issues.failure_explanation: In the proof of Theorem A.2, the claimed homotopy identity \eqref{eq:hohomo} fails, and the argument is circular. First, the proof claims that $\ker(\mcI^\vartriangle) = \operatorname{im}(\dDh)$ is an immediate consequence of (2.19) (`\eqref{eq:ii}`), but (2.19) is the identity for the differential variational bicomplex, and in Section 3 the difference analogue (3.17) is stated assuming the exactness of the difference variational bicomplex that Theorem A.2 is supposed to prove. Second, formula \eqref{eq:hohomo} is asserted to hold for all $k \in \{0, \dots, p\}$. For $k = p$, since $\Omega^{p+1,l} = 0$, \eqref{eq:hohomo} asserts $\dDh(h_\uph^{p,l}(\sigma)) = \sigma$ for all $\sigma \in \Omega^{p,l}$, which would imply that every $(p,l)$-form is horizontally exact and $\ker(\mcI^\vartriangle) = \Omega^{p,l}$ (so $\mathscr{F}^l = 0$), contradicting the definition and non-triviality of $\mathscr{F}^l$. Concretely, for $p=1$ and $\sigma = \Delta^1 \wedge \dv u^1 \in \Omega^{1,1}$, $\dDh \sigma = 0$ and $h_\uph^{1,1}(\sigma) = 0$ because $F^{i+1}(\partial_n \intp \sigma) = F^{i+1}(\dv u^1) = 0$ for all $i \ge 0$, so the left-hand side of \eqref{eq:hohomo} is $0$ while the right-hand side is $\Delta^1 \wedge \dv u^1 \neq 0$. The proof attempts to adapt Anderson's differential homotopy operator by replacing total derivatives with finite differences, but $(S - \id)$ is not a derivation and does not satisfy the differential Leibniz rule on which Anderson's homotopy relies.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the invalid homotopy construction in Theorem A.2 with an established discrete exactness proof (such as the combinatorial/algebraic difference Poincaré lemma techniques developed by Kupershmidt, Hydon--Mansfield, or Zharinov) and correct the homotopy identity at $k=p$ to properly incorporate the projection $\mcI^\vartriangle$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem A.2 fails completely to establish exactness of the augmented horizontal complex. Because Theorem A.3 explicitly relies on the projection property $\sigma = \mcI^\vartriangle(\sigma) + \dDh \tau$ provided by Theorem A.2, the proof of Theorem A.3 (the exactness of the difference boundary complex) is also invalidated.
issues.title: Invalid horizontal homotopy operator and false homotopy formula in proof of Theorem A.2
issues.why_classification: The purported proof of the central foundational theorem of the paper (exactness of the difference variational bicomplex) fails due to an invalid operator definition, a false homotopy identity, and circular reliance on the continuous bicomplex; repairing it requires importing or constructing an entirely different global proof architecture for discrete bicomplex exactness.
